case_title: VINOD KUMAR v. AMRITPAL @ CHHOTU & ORS.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.149; IPC s.304 Part II
trial_court_outcome: Convicted for offence punishable under Sections 302/149
neutral_facts: The accused, five individuals, were involved in an incident where the victim, a male, was forcibly taken into a vehicle. The accused then assaulted the victim, causing severe injuries including fractured ribs, a ruptured lung, and damage to the windpipe and liver. The victim was taken to a doctor but later died due to excessive bleeding and shock from the injuries. The accused then disposed of the victim's body in a canal. The prosecution presented medical evidence showing the injuries were on vital parts of the body, and eyewitness accounts confirmed the assault. The trial court convicted the accused for murder under Section 302 of the IPC, but the High Court reduced the charge to Section 304 Part II. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, restoring the original conviction for murder.
